summary: Get started no longer pre-picks how often you are paid, and its final summary now ticks the step you just finished. The spending line now separates what you typed from our guesses, and no Education tile shows for a retired household with no children. Extra taps on the questions no longer jump you past an answer.
points: Pay frequency starts unchosen and Continue asks you to pick one.
A fix button now selects the wrong digits in a year box.
Our guesses are no longer counted as spending you gave.
A choice in a question waits a moment so a double tap cannot skip it.
numbers: 5 older issues and 4 second-round issues closed

summary: A plan with pay but no accounts now gets the same next step on the Dashboard, Your plan, Get started, Next best action and the bottom row; before, they gave four different answers. Months of savings just over the goal now round up, such as 6.1 months, a bit over the 6 you want.
points: The All steps page says which question is next while the questions are under way.
The check-in names the first of several things left as the first.
numbers: 5 pages now agree on one next step

summary: On a very small phone (320 px wide) the Dashboard rows no longer push the main button off the screen. A month reopened in the check-in with no note stays among your months. Estate documents gives the guardian's name its own box and no longer treats an old free-text note as a chosen guardian.
points: The warning no longer pastes your old text back at you.
Needs attention shows a chosen guardian with a button to put the guardian in your will.

summary: The chance your money lasts is now the same on the Advisor's plan, Annuities and Chance the money lasts pages. Before, one page said 78% and another said 80% for the same plan, because each ran its own pretend futures.
points: When the Chance page already ran this plan, the others show its figure.
Otherwise both say about, rounded to the nearest 5.
The quoted-chance card measures its gap from the figure the table shows.

summary: On Get started, a question about a box now has a button that takes you to that box, such as Fix the rate. A Continue tap within 0.8 seconds of an ask is ignored so it cannot skip it. With only spending entered you see A few more answers will fill this in instead of a verdict on an emergency fund you never entered.
points: Jumping back by its address part way through returns to the question you reached.
The ask takes focus so a keyboard user lands in it.
numbers: 0.8 s guard against a double tap

summary: The notes that explain how the check-in, Dashboard, All steps and Estate documents pages work were brought up to date with the two rounds of fixes. Nothing on screen changes.
On a 320 px wide phone the Dashboard's check-in row pushed the Continue your plan button off a 568 px screen. Under 360 px wide the row now sits below the button.
The Health score page now shows one arrow on each step row, not two.
On Our guesses, kept lines used to leave over 500 px of blank space after three were settled. The row now holds its height only 0.7 seconds, then lets go, and the emptied card shrinks too.

In the check-in, a month that has ended now shows its next thing, such as save the month's net worth, as the filled button. Before, the page said one thing was left but gave no button. The Finish button stays outlined until nothing is left.

On an empty plan, Next best action and the check-in now both say Set up my plan, the same as the Dashboard and Get started. Before, one said Add what comes in and the check-in asked you to update balances you did not have.

Every page's quiet bottom row now reads Continue your plan: question 5 of 7 while the questions are under way; it used to say step 1 of 5 under a button saying question 5 of 7. A plan built on the pages gets Continue your plan: Enter what goes out on the Dashboard, Your plan and Get started.
numbers: question N of 7 on every page

summary: An older month reopened with a note is now reachable in the check-in; before, only this month and last showed. On Estate documents, after typing who would raise the children, the page now says who you chose and that a signed will must name them.
points: The button reads Put the guardian in your will.
Needs attention says the same.

summary: The All steps page said 2 of 6 steps done while also saying Do step 2. It now counts only steps you have passed, and the button reads Do step 2: Your month.
numbers: same rule as the next-step button

summary: On Your plan and Needs attention, 5.7 months of savings read 6 months beside build it to 6 months. Months short of the target are now never rounded up to it.

Your plan's rows for the month, cushion, retirement, take-out and required withdrawal no longer say pay, savings, Social Security or ages are missing when they are already on file. They name only what is really missing and link to the first.

Undoing or reopening a month in the check-in no longer deletes that month's note; it is kept and filled back in. The budget guide is named Spend less, save more everywhere, and Estate documents has one filled button while a paper's form is open.
points: The guardian's form asks Who would raise the children? first.
The button and Needs attention say Name a guardian in your will.

summary: A coin added with its purchase date can now be corrected on Holdings, and the cost follows what you paid. Fees with no holdings, Stocks by age with no holdings and the Bracket explorer no longer show confusing or false parts before you enter anything.
points: Stocks by age uses plain words in its legend and milestones.
The Bracket explorer shows no you are here until income is on file.
Fees keeps its advisory-fee fold closed.

summary: On the Money calendar, a saved payday dated in the future no longer blocks saving, and emptying a saved payday is refused in words. A W-2 reminder is no longer shown for a year with no salary. Spending's Ledger link was taken back out because it disagreed with the page's totals.

On the Money calendar, an old saved payday no longer blocks changing any other date; only boxes you changed are checked. A pension or Social Security paid twice a month now says the payer's days may differ. This closed a severity-5 problem found in review.

The Ledger now saves a 0.00 imported line with its category and treats a typed minus as money out. A new 0 line is refused with a message right above the Amount box. Import's Add the account button comes first and brings you back, and after Erase the Start a new plan button is the only filled one.
points: A Ledger link can show only money out or only money in, with Show money in and out.
An uncategorised view says how many lines go out.
Two outside problems were handed on: the unicode minus and (45.20) in amount reading.
